summary:
G7 countries agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel from emergency reserves after energy prices surged. The coordinated drawdown followed pressure from US President Donald Trump, who had threatened to cut off US diesel supplies and opposed export restrictions. The move is intended to address price spikes. In France, student protests over school standards have spread to more than 1,000 schools, with blockades and clashes with police. Ministers have called for a day of dialogue, while students have called for further strike action.

Russian attacks hit Kyiv’s Northern Bridge after repeated strikes on the Southern Bridge, the city’s mayor said. The Guardian also reported attacks on a school and a hospital as strikes on the capital’s infrastructure intensified. In a separate incident, the UAE said a co-pilot attacked the captain of a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv with a crash axe, in what officials described as an attempted terrorist attack. The assault halted direct service between Dubai and Tel Aviv; airlines are preparing to bring Israelis back from the UAE.

Spain’s parliament rejected two government housing measures, drawing protests outside. The proposals included automatic renewal of rental contracts and restrictions on evicting vulnerable tenants. North Korea launched a ballistic missile towards the sea from its east coast, South Korea and Japan said. The launch came a day after renewed dispute with Seoul over mines that injured South Korean soldiers near the border.

headlines.title: G7 agrees to release up to 100 million barrels of oil
headlines.summary: G7 countries agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel from emergency reserves. The coordinated move followed a surge in prices and US pressure to avoid restrictions on energy exports.

headlines.title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv’s bridges and other sites
headlines.summary: Russian attacks hit Kyiv’s Northern Bridge after repeated strikes on the Southern Bridge, the city’s mayor said. The Guardian also reported strikes on a school and a hospital as attacks on the capital’s infrastructure escalated.

headlines.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe, UAE says
headlines.summary: The UAE said a co-pilot used a crash axe to attack the captain of a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv in an attempted terrorist attack. The incident halted direct service between Dubai and Tel Aviv, and airlines are preparing to bring Israelis back from the UAE.

headlines.title: Student protests spread across France
headlines.summary: Student protests over school standards have spread across France, with blockades and clashes with police. More than 1,000 schools have been affected, while the government has called for a day of dialogue.

headlines.title: Spain’s parliament rejects housing measures
headlines.summary: Spain’s parliament rejected two government measures intended to make housing more affordable, prompting protests outside. The proposals included automatic renewal of rental contracts and limits on evicting vulnerable tenants.

headlines.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile towards the sea
headlines.summary: North Korea launched a ballistic missile towards the sea from its east coast, South Korea and Japan said. The launch came a day after renewed dispute with Seoul over mines that injured South Korean soldiers near the border.

headlines.title: Tigray rebels leave regional capital as forces advance
headlines.summary: Tigray rebels were abandoning Mekelle as pro-government forces advanced, according to local reports. The fighting has raised fears of a wider regional conflict, with foreign powers including Eritrea, Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia drawn in.
